question.problem:
The local truncation error (LTE) of a numerical method with step size $Δx$ is

$$
τ(Δx)=5(Δx)^{4}+3(Δx)^{5}.
$$

Complete the following sentences.

$\,$ With step size $Δx=0.6,$ the local truncation error is $≈$
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ With step size $Δx=0.3,$ the local truncation error is $≈$
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Decreasing from $Δx=0.6$ to $Δx=0.3,$ the LTE is reduced by a factor of $≈$
{{field-3}}.

$\,$ According to this data, the order of the method is approximately
{{field-4}}.
question.worked_solution:
A numerical method has order $p$ if $p$ is the largest positive integer such that the local truncation error (LTE) satisfies

$$
τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{p+1})\,\text{as}\,Δx\to 0.
$$

The order describes how fast errors shrink as $Δx$ decreases.

In other words, a numerical method has order $p$ if, for sufficiently small step sizes, reducing the step size by a factor of $k$ reduces the LTE by a factor of approximately ${k}^{p+1}.$

First, we compute the LTE for the given step sizes:

- With step size $Δx=0.6,$ the LTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}τ(0.6) & =5(0.6)^{4}+3(0.6)^{5} \\  & =5\cdot 0.129\,6+3\cdot 0.077\,76 \\  & =0.648+0.233\,28 \\  & =0.881\,28 \\  & ≈0.881.\end{aligned}
$$

- With step size $Δx=0.3,$ the LTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}τ(0.3) & =5(0.3)^{4}+3(0.3)^{5} \\  & =5\cdot 0.008\,1+3\cdot 0.002\,43 \\  & =0.0405+0.007\,29 \\  & =0.047\,79 \\  & ≈0.048.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the order by comparing the errors. The step size decreases from $0.6$ to $0.3.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
k=\frac{0.6}{0.3}=2.
$$

As a result, for a numerical method of order $p,$ the LTE should decrease by a factor of approximately

$$
{k}^{p+1}={2}^{p+1}.
$$

On the other hand, the LTE actually decreases from $0.881\,28$ to $0.047\,79.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
\frac{0.881\,28}{0.047\,79}=18.440\,67…≈18.441.
$$

Comparing the two scale factors for the LTE, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{p+1} & ≈18.440\,67… \\ p+1 & ≈{log}_{2}⁡(18.440\,67…) \\ p+1 & ≈4.204… \\ p & ≈3.204….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounding to the nearest integer, the estimated order of the method is
$3.$

Indeed, this coincides with the definition of the order from the expression for the LTE:

$$
τ(Δx)=5(Δx)^{4}+3(Δx)^{5}\,⇒\,τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{4})=O\,((Δx)^{3+1}),\,Δx\to 0.
$$

Hence, the order of the method is $3.$
